number_of_offences: Number of offences/counts charged: 2, Number finally upheld: 2
key_evidence_accepted: The evidence of PW9 (father of the deceased), the FIR lodged on the basis of the oral complaint made by the deceased at the police station, the subsequent statement of the deceased at the hospital as recorded by the I.O., the evidence of PWs 2 & 10 who corroborated the testimony of PW9, and the postmortem report and the evidence of Doctor-PW13 fully corroborates with the evidence of PW9.
witness_credibility: The testimony of father-PW9 inspired confidence and the chain of events and circumstantial evidence thereof completely supports his statements which in turn strengthens the prosecution case with no manner of doubt. His evidence was intrinsically reliable and wholly trustworthy.
trial_duration: Dates of offence: 18 May 2006; Trial judgment: 11 March 2015; High Court decision: 11 March 2015; Supreme Court decision: 15 May 2018
legal_representation: Counsel for the accused: Mohd. Aslam Goni, Syed Mehdi Imam, Atif Suhrawardy, Omar Siddiqui, Ms. Varnita Rastogi, Tabrez Ahmad; Counsel for the State: Ms. Fauzia Shakil, Ujjwal Singh, Mojahid Karim Khan, M. Shoeb Alam
investigation_status: FIR lodged on the basis of oral complaint made by deceased at police station; charge sheet filed; trial completed
appeal_history: Trial court: Acquittal; High Court: Conviction under s. 302/341 RPC; Supreme Court: Dismissed the appeal, upheld High Court's conviction
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the accused assaulted the deceased on his head with an iron rod, resulting in his death. The FIR lodged on the basis of the oral complaint made by the deceased at the police station was a reliable document. The subsequent statement of the deceased at the hospital was corroborated by PW-9 and other witnesses. The postmortem report and the evidence of Doctor-PW-13 fully corroborated the evidence of PW-9. The prosecution claimed that the accused's attack was the cause of the deceased's death and that the evidence of PW-9, though a close relative of the victim, was reliable and trustworthy.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the trial court adopted a hyper technical approach, leading to the acquittal of the accused. The accused contended that the entire case depended on the veracity of the evidence of PW-9, who was an interested witness and therefore his evidence was not reliable. The defence also argued that the High Court erred in reversing the trial court's order of acquittal and that the prosecution failed to prove the motive and the guilt of the accused beyond reasonable doubt.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the principle that the appellate court's power in an appeal against acquittal is the same as that in an appeal against conviction, but the presumption of innocence is in favor of the accused. The court emphasized that the High Court should only interfere if the appreciation of evidence was based on erroneous considerations or there was manifest illegality in the trial court's conclusion.
precedent_relied_upon: Dalip Singh & Ors. v. State of Punjab [1954] 1 SCR 145; Masalti v. State of U.P. [1964] 8 SCR 133; Harbans Kaur & Anr. v. State of Haryana 2005 CriLJ 2199; Padam Singh v. State of U.P. (2000) 1 SCC 621; Rathinam v. State of Tamil Nadu & Anr. (2011) 11 SCC 140; Bindeshwari Prasad Singh & Ors. v. State of Bihar & Anr. (2002) 6 SCC 650; Sunil Kumar Sambhudayal Gupta & Ors. v. State of Maharashtra (2010) 13 SCC 657; Shivaji Sahabrao Bobade & Anr. v. State of Maharashtra (1973) 2 SCC 793; State of U.P. v. Kishanpal & Ors. (2008) 16 SCC 73; Nallabothu Venkaiah v. State of Andhra Pradesh (2002) 7 SCC 117; Jarnail Singh & Ors. v. State of Punjab (2009) 9 SCC 719; Shivaji Genu Mohite v. State of Maharashtra AIR 1973 SC 55
sentencing_rationale: The final sentence was imposed because the High Court found that the prosecution successfully proved the guilt of the accused beyond reasonable doubt. The accused was convicted under Sections 302/341 of the Ranbir Penal Code and sentenced to life imprisonment and fines.
other_sentence_order: The accused was sentenced to suffer imprisonment for life and to pay a fine of Rs.1,000/- for the offence punishable under Section 302, RPC and to pay a fine of Rs.500/- for the offence under Section 341, RPC, with the direction to realize the fine amount from his estate.
